blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation in the Education & Research context — regulation-first design, a fixed delivery rhythm, and outcomes your board can audit.

In Education & Research, agentic ai & hyperautomation turns knowledge work into orchestrated autonomy. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: agentic process automation, digital workforce & multi-agent orchestration, decision intelligence systems — delivered on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: Advising, scheduling, accreditation evidence and grant reporting consume academic hours; support staff swim in document flows.
LMS, SIS, attendance and support-service data never meet; at-risk students surface at failure, not at drift.
Generative tools flood campuses with no policy infrastructure; detection arms races erode trust while legitimate assistive use goes ungoverned.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

7 services from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower make up the delivery pattern — Agentic Process Automation, Digital Workforce & Multi-Agent Orchestration, Decision Intelligence Systems, Intelligent Document Processing as the usual core — run through the Dataq Method with GDPR-K / minors' data rules obligations baked into the design from the first sprint.
Services we deploy in this sector

items: Agents that execute the work: tool-using, policy-bounded, and fully logged for audit.
Agents operated as one fleet: roles, queues, budgets and audit trails.
Decision paths that run in milliseconds, with policy checks and full logging.
Contracts, claims and invoices read end-to-end: extraction, validation and downstream action.
Early-warning signals trigger advising interventions with case management (retention lift in targeted cohorts)
Learning-outcome evidence assembled for program reviews (faculty reporting hours down)

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: GDPR-K / minors' data rules and Research ethics (IRB/ethics boards). Human-subject and data governance for research. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

This capability runs on the cadence set out below; the rhythm is fixed, the scope is signed. Weeks 1–2 are measurement only: we lock the current metric with your team and both sides sign it before a line of build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver a bounded pilot — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a named control owner on your side. Weeks 9–12 turn what worked into runbooks, monitoring and enablement, then report the measured delta against the baseline. A missed gate means a documented stop-or-redirect decision, not a quiet extension.
